old.F3: United States policy prioritizes capture of terrorist suspects over lethal action.
old.F4: A feasibility assessment of capture options is required as a component of any proposal for lethal action.
old.F5: Lethal action to prevent terrorist attacks against U.S. persons is limited to circumstances where capture is not feasible and no other reasonable alternative can effectively address the threat.
old.F6: Lethal action is not to be proposed or pursued as punishment or as a substitute for prosecution in civilian court or a military commission.
old.F7: Capture is preferred even when neither prosecution nor third-country custody is available as a disposition option at the time.

new.F3: United States policy guidance addresses the relative priority of capturing terrorist suspects and using lethal action.
new.F4: Capture options are relevant considerations in proposals for lethal action.
new.F5: Assessments of lethal action to prevent terrorist attacks against U.S. persons can involve whether capture is feasible and whether other reasonable alternatives can effectively address the threat.
new.F6: Lethal-action proposals may involve questions of punishment and prosecution in civilian court or a military commission.
new.F7: Neither prosecution nor third-country custody may be available as a disposition option at the time.
